questionBank.exp: The supplier registers with the financial institution or a third-party supply chain financing platform. The platform may require information about invoices and financial health. (Module 5B, Supply Chain Financing — Supplier Registration)

questionBank.q: An exporter has a confirmed L/C for USD 1,000,000. The exporter's bank provides a Packing Loan of USD 800,000. The loan is secured by:
opts: A. The exporter's assets
B. The confirmed L/C
C. The goods
D. The buyer's credit
questionBank.exp: A Packing Loan is secured by the incoming payment instrument (the L/C). The bank relies on the L/C for repayment. (Module 5B, Packing Loan)

questionBank.q: A factor provides credit protection to an exporter. This means that if the buyer defaults, the factor:
opts: A. Will not pay the exporter
B. Will pay the exporter up to the approved credit limit
C. Will sue the buyer
D. Will recover the goods
questionBank.exp: Credit protection in factoring means the factor covers the risk of buyer default up to the approved credit limit. This is a key benefit for the exporter. (Module 5B, Factoring)

questionBank.q: An exporter is using Factoring for the first time. The exporter's key benefit is:
opts: A. Access to cheaper financing
B. Outsourcing of credit functions, providing more time for core business
C. Guaranteed payment from the buyer
D. Lower cost than Forfaiting
questionBank.exp: Factoring allows the exporter to outsource credit functions (collection, credit protection, account management), providing more time to concentrate on core business activities. (Module 5B, Factoring benefits)

questionBank.q: A forfaiter purchases a series of promissory notes from an exporter. The notes are guaranteed by the importer's bank. The forfaiter bears:
opts: A. Only the currency risk
B. The credit risk of the importer's bank
C. The performance risk of the exporter
D. The shipping risk
questionBank.exp: In forfaiting, the forfaiter bears the credit risk of the importer's bank (which guaranteed the notes). The exporter is released from liability (without recourse). (Module 5B, Forfaiting)

questionBank.q: An exporter has received a Letter of Credit from a buyer. The exporter wants to use the L/C as security for pre-export financing. The bank providing the Packing Loan must verify:
opts: A. The exporter's credit rating
B. The genuineness of the L/C
C. The buyer's business history
D. The carrier's reliability
questionBank.exp: The bank must verify the genuineness of the L/C. The L/C is the security for the Packing Loan. (Module 5B, Packing Loan)

questionBank.q: In a Supply Chain Financing arrangement, the financial institution earns its profit from:
opts: A. The discount on early payment and fees
B. The interest charged to the buyer
C. The supplier's profit margin
D. The customs duties
questionBank.exp: The financial institution earns its profit from the fees and the difference between the early payment (discounted) and the full invoice amount paid at maturity. (Module 5B, Supply Chain Financing — Financial Institution's Role)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a key benefit of Supply Chain Financing for suppliers?
opts: A. Higher interest rates
B. Improved cash flow and reduced financial stress
C. Longer payment terms
D. Guaranteed sales
questionBank.exp: Suppliers benefit from improved cash flow and reduced financial stress. They also access better financing terms than traditional lenders would offer. (Module 5B, Supply Chain Financing — Supplier Benefits)

questionBank.q: An exporter has shipped goods and the buyer's bank has accepted a Bill of Exchange drawn by the exporter. The exporter discounts the Banker's Acceptance with a discount house. The discount rate is lower than a Trade Acceptance because:
opts: A. Banker's Acceptances are larger
B. Banker's Acceptances carry lower credit risk
C. Trade Acceptances are not negotiable
D. Banker's Acceptances have longer tenors
questionBank.exp: Banker's Acceptances carry the credit of a bank, which has lower credit risk than a corporate buyer. This makes the discount rate lower. (Module 2.3, and Module 5B)

questionBank.q: An exporter in China has a factoring arrangement for sales to the USA. The export factor advances funds and the import factor collects from the buyer. The exporter's bank is not involved in collection. This arrangement:
opts: A. Is unusual in international trade
B. Is a standard factoring arrangement
C. Cannot be used for exports
D. Requires a confirmed L/C
questionBank.exp: Factoring with export and import factors is a standard arrangement in international trade. The export factor advances funds, and the import factor handles collection. (Module 5B, Factoring dynamics)

questionBank.q: A forfaiting transaction typically involves the sale of medium-term receivables. The key risk for the forfaiter is:
opts: A. The exporter may not ship the goods
B. The importer's bank may not honour its guarantee
C. The carrier may lose the goods
D. The buyer may reject the goods
questionBank.exp: The forfaiter's primary risk is the credit risk of the importer's bank (or the guarantor). If the guarantor defaults, the forfaiter bears the loss. (Module 5B, Forfaiting)

questionBank.q: An exporter is preparing to ship goods and needs financing. The exporter has a confirmed L/C. The bank provides a Packing Loan. The loan is repaid from:
opts: A. The exporter's other assets
B. The proceeds of the L/C
C. The exporter's profits
D. The buyer's advance payment
questionBank.exp: A Packing Loan is repaid from the proceeds of the L/C. When the L/C is paid, the bank deducts the loan amount and remits the balance to the exporter. (Module 5B, Packing Loan)

questionBank.q: A trade dispute arises between two countries over alleged dumping of steel. The complaining country wants to resolve the matter through a formal international process. Which organization provides the framework for resolving such trade disputes?
opts: A. UNCTAD
B. World Trade Organization (WTO)
C. International Chamber of Commerce (ICC)
D. AfCFTA
questionBank.exp: The WTO's Dispute Settlement Understanding provides a formal procedure for resolving trade quarrels between member countries. This is a key function of the WTO. (Module 6.1, WTO — Dispute Settlement)

questionBank.q: The WTO was established on January 1, 1995, following the Uruguay Round of negotiations. Which agreement preceded the WTO and regulated world trade since 1948?
opts: A. The Bretton Woods Agreement
B. The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
C. The Treaty of Rome
D. The North American Free Trade Agreement
questionBank.exp: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) regulated world trade from 1948 until the WTO was established in 1995. GATT was an informal organization, unlike the WTO which is a permanent institution. (Module 6.1, WTO — Formation)

questionBank.q: A developing country is negotiating to join the WTO. The country is concerned about implementing all WTO agreements immediately. The WTO provides:
opts: A. No flexibility for developing countries
B. Some flexibility in implementing commitments for developing countries
C. The same requirements for all members
D. Special treatment only for least-developed countries
questionBank.exp: The WTO system gives developing countries some flexibility in implementing their commitments. This is built into the WTO agreements. (Module 6.1, WTO — Functions)

questionBank.q: A country is concerned that another member is not complying with its WTO commitments. The country can initiate dispute settlement proceedings. The first step in the WTO dispute settlement process is:
opts: A. A panel ruling
B. Consultation between the parties
C. An appeal to the Appellate Body
D. Trade sanctions
questionBank.exp: The WTO dispute settlement system encourages countries to settle their differences through consultation first. Failing that, they can follow a staged procedure including panel rulings and appeals. (Module 6.1, WTO — Dispute Settlement)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an objective of the WTO as stated in the course material?
opts: A. To promote protectionism
B. To improve the standard of living of people in member countries
C. To increase tariffs on imported goods
D. To establish a world government
questionBank.exp: Improving the standard of living of people in member countries is one of the WTO's stated objectives. Other objectives include full employment, increased trade of goods and services, and protection of the environment. (Module 6.1, WTO — Objectives)

questionBank.q: The WTO's top-level decision-making body is the Ministerial Conference. How often does the Ministerial Conference typically meet?
opts: A. Annually
B. At least once in every two years
C. Every five years
D. Only when disputes arise
questionBank.exp: The WTO's Ministerial Conference meets at least once in every two years. It is the top-level decision-making body. (Module 6.1, WTO — Structure)

questionBank.q: A country is accused of violating intellectual property rights under a WTO agreement. Which WTO agreement deals with intellectual property protection?
opts: A. GATT
B. GATS
C. TRIPs
D. DSU
questionBank.exp: TRIPs (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights) is the WTO agreement that sets rules for protecting copyrights, patents, trademarks, and other intellectual property. (Module 6.1, WTO — Intellectual Property)

questionBank.q: A country wants to open its banking sector to foreign competition. Which WTO agreement governs trade in services like banking and insurance?
opts: A. GATT
B. GATS
C. TRIPs
D. DSU
questionBank.exp: GATS (General Agreement on Trade in Services) sets the principles for trade in services, including banking, insurance, telecommunications, tourism, and transport. (Module 6.1, WTO — Services)

questionBank.q: The WTO's Trade Policy Review Mechanism requires all members to undergo periodic scrutiny. The purpose of this review is:
opts: A. To punish non-compliant members
B. To improve transparency and understanding of policies
C. To impose tariffs
D. To resolve disputes
questionBank.exp: The Trade Policy Review Mechanism's purpose is to improve transparency, create a greater understanding of policies, and assess their impact. Many members see the reviews as constructive feedback. (Module 6.1, WTO — Policy Review)

questionBank.q: UNCTAD was established in 1964. Which of the following was a key concern that led to the creation of UNCTAD?
opts: A. Concerns of developed countries over market access
B. Concerns of developing countries over the international market and great disparity with developed nations
C. Concerns over the World Trade Organization's effectiveness
D. Concerns over European integration
questionBank.exp: UNCTAD was established based on concerns of developing countries over the international market, multi-national corporations, and the great disparity between developed and developing nations. It provides a forum for developing countries to discuss economic development issues. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD)

questionBank.q: A developing country wants to export manufactured goods to developed countries at reduced tariff rates. Under which UNCTAD program does this benefit apply?
opts: A. The Generalized System of Preferences (GSP)
B. The World Trade Organization
C. The International Chamber of Commerce
D. The African Continental Free Trade Area
questionBank.exp: The Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) was conceived and implemented by UNCTAD. It allows exports of manufactured goods from developing countries to enter developed countries duty-free or at reduced rates. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD — GSP)

questionBank.q: A developed country is considering whether to grant tariff preferences to imports from a developing country under the GSP scheme. The GSP was initiated by:
opts: A. The WTO
B. The IMF
C. UNCTAD
D. The World Bank
questionBank.exp: UNCTAD conceived and implemented the Generalized System of Preferences (GSP). One of UNCTAD's principal achievements has been to promote this system. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD — GSP)

questionBank.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between GATT and the WTO?
opts: A. GATT replaced the WTO
B. The WTO replaced GATT, and GATT is now the WTO's principal rule-book for trade in goods
C. GATT and WTO are the same organization
D. The WTO is a regional agreement under GATT
questionBank.exp: The Uruguay Round (1986-93) led to the creation of the WTO. GATT is now the WTO's principal rule-book for trade in goods, but the WTO covers services and intellectual property as well. (Module 6.1, WTO — Formation and Agreements)

questionBank.q: A business association wants to establish voluntary rules for international trade documentation and dispute resolution. Which organization is most likely to provide these rules?
opts: A. WTO
B. UNCTAD
C. International Chamber of Commerce (ICC)
D. AfCFTA
questionBank.exp: The ICC performs three primary activities: establishment of rules (like UCP and URC), dispute resolution (International Court of Arbitration), and policy advocacy. (Module 6.3, ICC — Aims and Objectives)

questionBank.q: A company in Nigeria wants to expand its exports to other African countries. The company learns about a trade agreement that aims to create a single market for goods and services across Africa. This agreement is:
opts: A. ECOWAS
B. AfCFTA
C. COMESA
D. SADC
questionBank.exp: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) aims to create a single market for goods and services, promote intra-Africa trade, and accelerate economic integration across Africa. It was launched on January 1, 2021. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA)

questionBank.q: A small business in Ghana wants to export to Kenya under the AfCFTA. The business is excited about the opportunities but is concerned about infrastructure deficiencies and regulatory barriers. These concerns represent:
opts: A. Benefits of AfCFTA
B. Challenges of AfCFTA
C. Objectives of AfCFTA
D. Reasons to avoid AfCFTA
questionBank.exp: Challenges such as infrastructure deficiencies, regulatory barriers, and the need for investment in productive sectors must be addressed for AfCFTA's full potential to be realized. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Challenges)

questionBank.q: The ICC was founded in Paris, France in 1919. Which of the following is NOT a primary activity of the ICC?
opts: A. Establishment of rules
B. Dispute resolution
C. Policy advocacy
D. Enforcement of trade sanctions
questionBank.exp: The ICC's three primary activities are establishment of rules, dispute resolution, and policy advocacy. The ICC does not enforce trade sanctions — that is a government function. (Module 6.3, ICC — Aims and Objectives)

questionBank.q: A company involved in international trade wants to understand the rules governing documentary credits. The ICC has published a set of rules that are widely used. These rules are:
opts: A. UCP 600
B. GATT
C. GATS
D. URC 522
questionBank.exp: The ICC publishes the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600), which governs letters of credit. The ICC also publishes the URC 522 for collections. (Module 6.3, ICC — Rule-making)

questionBank.q: The ICC's International Court of Arbitration was established in 1923. This court:
opts: A. Is a government court
B. Provides arbitration services for international commercial disputes
C. Enforces trade sanctions
D. Issues trade regulations
questionBank.exp: The ICC's International Court of Arbitration provides arbitration services for international commercial disputes. It is one of the ICC's primary dispute resolution mechanisms. (Module 6.3, ICC — History)

questionBank.q: A country is considering joining the AfCFTA. The country's government wants to understand the primary objective of the agreement. The primary objective is:
opts: A. To establish a common currency
B. To create a single continental market for goods and services
C. To harmonize tax systems
D. To create a political union
questionBank.exp: The primary goal of AfCFTA is to boost economic growth, reduce poverty, and enhance industrialization and diversification by creating a single continental market for goods and services. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Objectives)

questionBank.q: The WTO has nearly 153 members accounting for over 97% of world trade. Decisions in the WTO are typically made by:
opts: A. Majority vote
B. Consensus
C. The Director-General
D. The General Council
questionBank.exp: Decisions in the WTO are typically made by consensus. While a majority vote is possible, it has never been used in the WTO and was extremely rare under GATT. (Module 6.1, WTO — Structure)

questionBank.q: A country's trade policies are being reviewed under the WTO's Trade Policy Review Mechanism. Which of the following is true about this review?
opts: A. Only developed countries are reviewed
B. All WTO members must undergo periodic scrutiny
C. The reviews are only for dispute resolution
D. The reviews are optional
questionBank.exp: All WTO members must undergo periodic scrutiny under the Trade Policy Review Mechanism. Each review contains reports by the country concerned and the WTO Secretariat. (Module 6.1, WTO — Policy Review)

questionBank.q: UNCTAD has 195 member states and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. What is the primary objective of UNCTAD?
opts: A. To regulate international trade tariffs
B. To maximize the trade, investment and development opportunities of developing countries
C. To enforce trade sanctions
D. To create a single global market
questionBank.exp: UNCTAD's goal is to maximize the trade, investment and development opportunities of developing countries and assist them in integrating into the world economy on an equitable basis. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD)

questionBank.q: A business wants to understand the rules for international trade documentation. The ICC's rules are voluntary but widely followed. This is because:
opts: A. They are legally enforceable by the UN
B. They are incorporated into thousands of daily transactions
C. They are mandatory under WTO rules
D. They are government regulations
questionBank.exp: While ICC rules are voluntary, thousands of daily transactions abide by the ICC-established rules as part of regular international trade. The ICC has unparalleled authority in setting rules for cross-border business. (Module 6.3, ICC)

questionBank.q: The AfCFTA was officially launched on January 1, 2021. What is a key opportunity presented by the AfCFTA for African businesses?
opts: A. Access to a larger market and ability to boost exports
B. Guaranteed government contracts
C. Lower taxes
D. Free trade with non-African countries
questionBank.exp: AfCFTA presents opportunities for African businesses to access a larger market, boost exports, and diversify their economies. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Opportunities)

questionBank.q: A dispute arises between two WTO members over agricultural subsidies. The complaining country initiates dispute settlement proceedings. After consultation fails, what is the next step in the WTO dispute settlement process?
opts: A. Trade sanctions
B. A panel ruling by independent experts
C. An appeal to the WTO General Council
D. Arbitration by the ICC
questionBank.exp: After consultation fails, the dispute follows a stage-by-stage procedure that includes a ruling by a panel of experts, with the chance to appeal the ruling on legal grounds. (Module 6.1, WTO — Dispute Settlement)

questionBank.q: A developing country is concerned that its exports may be affected by developed countries' standards. Under which WTO agreement can the developing country raise concerns about product standards?
opts: A. GATS
B. TRIPs
C. GATT (specifically the annexes on product standards)
D. The Dispute Settlement Understanding
questionBank.exp: GATT has annexes dealing with product standards (among other issues). These annexes are part of the WTO's umbrella agreement for trade in goods. (Module 6.1, WTO — Goods)

questionBank.q: UNCTAD's Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) allows developing countries to export manufactured goods to developed countries at reduced tariff rates. This benefit is designed to:
opts: A. Compensate developed countries for tariff losses
B. Promote exports from developing countries
C. Reduce imports into developing countries
D. Harmonize global tariffs
questionBank.exp: GSP was designed to promote exports of manufactured goods from developing countries by offering special tariff concessions. This gives developing countries a competitive advantage. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD — GSP)

questionBank.q: A company in Africa wants to expand exports to other African countries. The company hears about AfCFTA but is concerned about infrastructure deficiencies. This concern is:
opts: A. A challenge that must be addressed for the agreement's full potential
B. A reason to reject the agreement
C. Not relevant to trade
D. Only a concern for landlocked countries
questionBank.exp: Infrastructure deficiencies are a key challenge for AfCFTA. They must be addressed for the agreement's full potential to be realized. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Challenges)

questionBank.q: The ICC's vast networks of committees and experts keep members informed of issues affecting their industries. The ICC also maintains contact with:
opts: A. Only the WTO
B. The United Nations, WTO, and other intergovernmental agencies
C. National governments only
D. Regional trade blocs only
questionBank.exp: The ICC maintains contact with the United Nations, the World Trade Organization, and other intergovernmental agencies. This ensures business perspectives are represented at international level. (Module 6.3, ICC)

questionBank.q: A WTO member country has been found to have violated its commitments. The Dispute Settlement Understanding allows for:
opts: A. The complaining country to impose trade sanctions
B. A panel ruling and the possibility of an appeal
C. The WTO to impose fines
D. The case to be referred to the ICC
questionBank.exp: The WTO dispute settlement procedure includes a panel ruling and the chance to appeal the ruling on legal grounds. Confidence in the system is borne out by the number of cases brought to the WTO. (Module 6.1, WTO — Dispute Settlement)

questionBank.q: A country is considering joining the WTO. The country's parliament must ratify the WTO agreements. This requirement reflects that:
opts: A. WTO agreements are optional
B. WTO agreements have been ratified in all members' parliaments
C. WTO agreements are not legally binding
D. WTO agreements are only for developed countries
questionBank.exp: WTO agreements have been ratified in all members' parliaments. This gives the agreements domestic legal force in member countries. (Module 6.1, WTO — Structure)

questionBank.q: A developing country wants to export textiles to developed countries under the GSP scheme. The developed country offers reduced tariffs on textiles from developing countries. This is an example of:
opts: A. A WTO dispute settlement outcome
B. UNCTAD's GSP program
C. The ICC's model rules
D. AfCFTA's provisions
questionBank.exp: The GSP scheme, conceived and implemented by UNCTAD, offers special tariff concessions to exports from developing countries. This is a key UNCTAD achievement. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD — GSP)

questionBank.q: The WTO's General Council performs multiple roles, including meeting as the Trade Policy Review Body and the Dispute Settlement Body. The General Council consists of:
opts: A. Ministers from member countries
B. Ambassadors and heads of delegation (and sometimes officials from capitals)
C. Business leaders
D. UN representatives
questionBank.exp: The General Council normally consists of ambassadors and heads of delegation in Geneva, but sometimes officials sent from members' capitals. It meets several times a year at WTO headquarters. (Module 6.1, WTO — Structure)

questionBank.q: A business in Nigeria wants to export to Kenya under AfCFTA. The business owner is excited about the opportunities but recognizes the need for investment in productive sectors. This need represents:
opts: A. An opportunity created by AfCFTA
B. A challenge to realizing AfCFTA's full potential
C. A reason to delay exports
D. A requirement that only applies to large businesses
questionBank.exp: The need for investment in productive sectors is one of the challenges identified for AfCFTA's full potential to be realized. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Challenges)

questionBank.q: A company involved in international trade is facing a dispute with a foreign partner. The company wants to use arbitration services. Which ICC body provides these services?
opts: A. The World Council
B. The International Court of Arbitration
C. The Executive Board
D. The Finance Committee
questionBank.exp: The ICC's International Court of Arbitration was formed in 1923 and provides arbitration services for international commercial disputes. (Module 6.3, ICC — History and Governing Bodies)

questionBank.q: The ICC's World Council is the lead governing body. The World Council is composed of:
opts: A. National committee representatives
B. Individual business members
C. Government officials
D. UN representatives
questionBank.exp: The World Council is the ICC's lead governing body and is composed of national committee representatives. The chair and vice-chair are elected by the World Council every two years. (Module 6.3, ICC — Governing Bodies)

questionBank.q: A business association wants to advocate for open markets and the free flow of capital. Which organization's aims align most closely with these objectives?
opts: A. UNCTAD
B. WTO
C. International Chamber of Commerce (ICC)
D. AfCFTA
questionBank.exp: The ICC aims to foster international trade and commerce to promote and protect open markets for goods and services and the free flow of capital. (Module 6.3, ICC — Aims and Objectives)

questionBank.q: UNCTAD is part of the United Nations Secretariat dealing with trade, investment, and development issues. UNCTAD reports to:
opts: A. The WTO
B. The UN General Assembly and UN Economic and Social Council
C. The ICC
D. The World Bank
questionBank.exp: UNCTAD reports to the UN General Assembly and United Nations Economic and Social Council. It was established by the UN General Assembly in 1964. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD)

questionBank.q: A country is concerned about the effects of multi-national corporations on its economy. The country wants a forum to discuss these concerns with other developing countries. Which organization provides such a forum?
opts: A. WTO
B. UNCTAD
C. ICC
D. AfCFTA
questionBank.exp: UNCTAD was established to provide a forum where developing countries could discuss problems relating to their economic development, including concerns about multi-national corporations. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD — Background)

questionBank.q: The ICC's rules are voluntary, yet they are widely used in international trade. This is because ICC rules:
opts: A. Are legally binding in all countries
B. Provide practical, widely accepted standards
C. Are enforced by the WTO
D. Are required by the United Nations
questionBank.exp: The ICC has unparalleled authority in setting rules that govern cross-border business because its members engage in international business. The rules provide practical, widely accepted standards. (Module 6.3, ICC)

questionBank.q: A developed country is considering tariff reductions for imports from a developing country. The developed country wants to promote exports from the developing country. Which UNCTAD program supports this objective?
opts: A. The Generalized System of Preferences (GSP)
B. The Trade and Development Report
C. The World Investment Report
D. The Digital Economy Report
questionBank.exp: The GSP program supports this objective. It was conceived by UNCTAD to promote exports of manufactured goods from developing countries by offering special tariff concessions. (Module 6.2, UNCTAD — GSP)

questionBank.q: A country is concerned about the environmental impact of trade. The WTO's objectives include:
opts: A. Ignoring environmental concerns
B. Protecting the environment
C. Promoting only economic growth
D. Opposing environmental regulations
questionBank.exp: Protecting the environment is one of the WTO's stated objectives. The WTO also accepts the concept of sustainable development. (Module 6.1, WTO — Objectives)

questionBank.q: The ICC's Executive Board provides strategic direction for the organization. The Executive Board is elected by:
opts: A. The World Council
B. The International Court of Arbitration
C. The Finance Committee
D. National committees
questionBank.exp: The Executive Board is elected by the World Council and is comprised of 30 business leaders and ex-officio members. It develops ICC strategies and implements policy. (Module 6.3, ICC — Governing Bodies)

questionBank.q: A country wants to promote intra-Africa trade and diversify its economy. The country participates in AfCFTA. What is the primary goal of AfCFTA?
opts: A. To increase tariffs on non-African goods
B. To boost economic growth and reduce poverty through a single continental market
C. To create a common African currency
D. To harmonize all African laws
questionBank.exp: The primary goal of AfCFTA is to boost economic growth, reduce poverty, and enhance the industrialization and diversification of African economies by creating a single continental market for goods and services. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Objectives)

questionBank.q: A dispute resolution expert wants to understand the ICC's dispute resolution mechanisms. The ICC's International Court of Arbitration was established in:
questionBank.exp: The ICC's International Court of Arbitration was formed in 1923, four years after the ICC was founded in 1919. (Module 6.3, ICC — History)

questionBank.q: A developing country is concerned that its exports may be subject to unfair competition. The country can raise concerns under the WTO's dispute settlement system. How many dispute cases were brought to the WTO in its first eight years?
opts: A. Around 10
B. Around 50
C. Around 150
D. Around 300
questionBank.exp: Confidence in the WTO dispute settlement system is reflected in the number of cases brought — around 300 cases in eight years, compared to 300 disputes during the entire life of GATT (1947-94). (Module 6.1, WTO — Dispute Settlement)

questionBank.q: A business wants to ensure its trade documents comply with international standards. The ICC provides voluntary rules that govern cross-border business. These rules are:
opts: A. Legally enforceable in all countries
B. Widely followed in daily international transactions
C. Only for large corporations
D. Only for banks
questionBank.exp: ICC rules are voluntary but are followed in thousands of daily transactions as part of regular international trade. The ICC has unparalleled authority in setting rules for cross-border business. (Module 6.3, ICC)

questionBank.q: A country is considering joining AfCFTA. The country's government wants to understand the opportunities. Which of the following is an opportunity presented by AfCFTA?
opts: A. Access to a larger market and ability to boost exports
B. Reduced infrastructure requirements
C. Guaranteed access to funding
D. Elimination of all regulations
questionBank.exp: AfCFTA presents opportunities for African businesses to access a larger market, boost exports, and diversify their economies. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Opportunities)

questionBank.q: The ICC has four primary governing bodies: the World Council, the Executive Board, the International Secretariat, and the Finance Committee. Which body is the operational arm of the ICC?
opts: A. The World Council
B. The Executive Board
C. The International Secretariat
D. The Finance Committee
questionBank.exp: The International Secretariat is the operational arm of the ICC. It is responsible for developing and implementing the ICC's work program and introducing business perspectives to intergovernmental organizations. (Module 6.3, ICC — Governing Bodies)

questionBank.q: A country wants to increase intra-Africa trade. Historically, intra-Africa trade has been low compared to other regions. AfCFTA aims to address this by:
opts: A. Eliminating tariff and non-tariff barriers
B. Increasing tariffs on non-African goods
C. Creating a common currency
D. Establishing a single government
questionBank.exp: AfCFTA aims to increase intra-Africa trade by eliminating tariff barriers, non-tariff barriers, and other trade barriers. This is a key objective. (Module 6.4, AfCFTA — Objectives)

questionBank.q: A business association wants to have its voice heard in international trade policy. The ICC maintains contact with the United Nations, the WTO, and other intergovernmental agencies. This ensures:
opts: A. ICC rules are legally binding
B. Business perspectives are represented at international level
C. ICC members have voting rights in the UN
D. ICC rules are enforced by the UN
questionBank.exp: The ICC maintains contact with the United Nations, the WTO, and other intergovernmental agencies to ensure business perspectives are represented in international policy discussions. (Module 6.3, ICC)

questionBank.q: A buyer in Nigeria has issued a Transferable Letter of Credit for EUR 100,000 in favour of London Maple Trading Company (a UK-based middleman). The L/C is for 5,000 pairs of moccasins at EUR 20 per pair. London Maple Trading Company requests the transferring bank (TD Bank) to transfer EUR 75,000 to XYZ Supplier Germany, stating the same quantity of goods (5,000 pairs) but at EUR 15 per pair. TD Bank advises the transfer to XYZ Supplier Germany. XYZ Supplier Germany ships the goods and presents documents for EUR 75,000. What is the middleman's profit in this transaction?
questionBank.exp: The middleman (London Maple Trading Company) receives EUR 100,000 from the buyer's bank and pays the manufacturer EUR 75,000. The difference of EUR 25,000 is the middleman's profit. This is the classic transferable L/C mechanism. (Sample case, Transferable L/C)

questionBank.q: In the transferable L/C scenario involving ABC Buyer, London Maple Trading Company, XYZ Supplier Germany, and TD Bank, which party is the First Beneficiary?
opts: A. ABC Buyer
B. London Maple Trading Company
C. XYZ Supplier Germany
D. TD Bank
questionBank.exp: The First Beneficiary is the party in whose favour the original L/C is issued — in this case, London Maple Trading Company. The Second Beneficiary is XYZ Supplier Germany (the manufacturer). (Sample case, Transferable L/C)

questionBank.q: In the transferable L/C scenario, XYZ Supplier Germany (the Second Beneficiary) ships the goods and presents documents to TD Bank for EUR 75,000. TD Bank notifies London Maple Trading Company of the presentation. London Maple Trading Company presents its own invoice and draft showing a value of EUR 100,000. TD Bank substitutes these documents for those of XYZ Supplier Germany and forwards them to the Nigerian Issuing Bank. What is the key risk that London Maple Trading Company bears in this arrangement?
opts: A. The buyer may not pay
B. XYZ Supplier Germany may fail to ship conforming goods
C. TD Bank may not transfer the funds
D. The Nigerian Issuing Bank may refuse the documents
questionBank.exp: London Maple Trading Company (First Beneficiary) bears the performance risk of XYZ Supplier Germany (Second Beneficiary). If the manufacturer fails to ship the goods or ships non-conforming goods, the middleman cannot present documents under the original L/C. (Module 3.7, Transferable L/C risks)

questionBank.q: In the transferable L/C scenario, TD Bank receives EUR 100,000 from the Nigerian Issuing Bank. TD Bank pays XYZ Supplier Germany EUR 75,000 and London Maple Trading Company EUR 25,000. Which of the following best describes TD Bank's role in this transaction?
opts: A. Issuing Bank
B. Advising Bank
C. Transferring Bank and Paying Bank
D. Confirming Bank
questionBank.exp: TD Bank acts as the Transferring Bank (handling the transfer of the L/C to the Second Beneficiary) and the Paying Bank (paying both beneficiaries). It facilitates the substitution of documents and disburses funds to both parties. (Module 3.4, Transferable L/C)

questionBank.q: A middleman receives a Transferable L/C from a buyer for EUR 100,000. The middleman wants to transfer the L/C to a manufacturer for EUR 75,000. However, the original L/C is not marked 'Transferable'. What should the middleman do?
opts: A. Proceed with the transfer anyway
B. Request the buyer to have the L/C amended to make it transferable
C. Use the L/C as collateral to open a Back-to-Back L/C
D. Abandon the transaction
questionBank.exp: A Letter of Credit must be specifically marked 'Transferable' to be transferred. If it is not, the middleman must request the buyer to have the L/C amended. Alternatively, the middleman could use a Back-to-Back L/C arrangement if the buyer is unwilling to amend. (Module 3.4, Transferable L/C)

questionBank.q: A middleman is comparing a Transferable L/C and a Back-to-Back L/C. The middleman receives a Transferable L/C for EUR 100,000 and transfers EUR 75,000 to a manufacturer. Under a Back-to-Back L/C, the middleman would use the EUR 100,000 L/C as security to open a separate L/C for EUR 75,000. Which of the following is a key difference in terms of the middleman's liability?
opts: A. In a Transferable L/C, the middleman bears less risk
B. In a Back-to-Back L/C, the middleman bears less risk
C. Both arrangements carry identical risk
D. The middleman bears no risk in either arrangement
questionBank.exp: A Transferable L/C offers more security for the First Beneficiary (middleman) because it is a single elongated transaction with the original applicant involved. A Back-to-Back L/C involves two separate L/Cs, which increases risk for the middleman. (Module 3.4, Transferable L/C vs Back-to-Back L/C)

questionBank.q: In the transferable L/C scenario, XYZ Supplier Germany (Second Beneficiary) ships 5,000 pairs of moccasins. However, the goods do not meet the quality standards specified in the original L/C. London Maple Trading Company cannot present documents under the original L/C. Which party bears the loss?
opts: A. ABC Buyer
B. London Maple Trading Company
C. XYZ Supplier Germany
D. TD Bank
questionBank.exp: The First Beneficiary (London Maple Trading Company) bears the performance risk of the Second Beneficiary (XYZ Supplier Germany). If the manufacturer ships non-conforming goods, the middleman cannot satisfy the terms of the original L/C and bears the loss. (Module 3.7, Transferable L/C risks)

questionBank.q: A middleman receives a Transferable L/C and transfers it to a secondary beneficiary. The secondary beneficiary presents documents that are compliant. The first beneficiary substitutes its own invoice for a higher amount. The bank pays the first beneficiary the higher amount and the second beneficiary the lower amount. The first beneficiary's profit is the difference. This mechanism is allowed under:
opts: A. UCP 600 Article 38
B. UCP 600 Article 14
C. UCP 600 Article 7
D. UCP 600 Article 18
questionBank.exp: UCP 600 Article 38 governs Transferable L/Cs. It allows the first beneficiary to substitute its own invoice and draft for those of the second beneficiary, keeping the difference as profit. (Module 3.4, Transferable L/C, and UCP Article 38)

questionBank.q: A buyer in Nigeria has a Transferable L/C issued in favour of London Maple Trading Company. TD Bank is the transferring bank. The transfer instruction specifies that the L/C is transferred to XYZ Supplier Germany with the same terms and conditions except for the value and unit price. What other terms can typically be reduced in a transfer?
opts: A. The description of goods
B. The latest shipment date and presentation period
C. The applicant's name
D. The place of expiry
questionBank.exp: In a Transferable L/C, the value, tenor, latest shipment date, and presentation period can be reduced or curtailed. The description of goods cannot be changed. (Module 3.4, Transferable L/C)

questionBank.q: In the transferable L/C scenario, TD Bank (the transferring bank) advises the transfer to XYZ Supplier Germany. XYZ Supplier Germany (Second Beneficiary) presents documents in accordance with the transferred L/C. TD Bank examines the documents and finds them compliant. However, London Maple Trading Company (First Beneficiary) fails to present its substitute invoice within the required timeframe. What should TD Bank do?
opts: A. Reject the presentation entirely
B. Pay XYZ Supplier Germany directly and notify London Maple Trading Company
C. Forward the original documents to the issuing bank without substitution
D. Return the documents to XYZ Supplier Germany
questionBank.exp: Under UCP 600 Article 38, if the First Beneficiary fails to present its substitute documents within the required timeframe, the transferring bank may deliver the Second Beneficiary's documents directly to the issuing bank. The First Beneficiary loses its right to the difference. (Module 3.4, Transferable L/C, and UCP Article 38)
